T.topic_fa: پنج ستاره‌ی کامل کمتر می‌فروشد: عیبی که خودتان نشان می‌دهید، برندتان را باورپذیر می‌کند
T.topic_en: A perfect five stars sells less: the flaw you show is what makes your brand believable
T.central_tension_fa: عیب را پنهان می‌کنیم تا قابل‌اعتماد به نظر برسیم؛ همین پنهان کردن ما را باورنکردنی می‌کند. پژوهش مرکز اشپیگل (نورث‌وسترن) نشان داد احتمال خرید معمولاً در امتیاز ۴ تا ۴٫۷ به اوج می‌رسد و نزدیک ۵ افت می‌کند. داو امسال ۵۰ نقد اولِ ردیت را بی‌ویرایش روی تبلیغش گذاشت، حتی «بوی شامپوی تاریخ‌گذشته‌ی هتل می‌دهد». اما شرط دارد: در آزمایش ۱۹۶۶، قهوه ریختنِ آدمِ توانا او را دوست‌داشتنی‌تر کرد و آدمِ معمولی را نه. به نظر من عیب فقط وقتی کمک می‌کند که کیفیت از قبل معلوم باشد.
T.central_tension_en: We hide the flaw to look trustworthy, and the hiding is what makes us unbelievable. Spiegel Research Center (Northwestern) found purchase likelihood typically peaks at ratings of 4.0-4.7 and drops as they approach 5.0. This year Dove printed the first 50 Reddit reviews of a hair mask unedited, including 'it kinda smells like expired hotel shampoo'. But there's a condition: in the 1966 pratfall study, spilling coffee made a highly capable candidate more likeable and an average one less. My take: a flaw only helps once your competence is already obvious.
T.working_hook_fa: پنج ستاره‌ی کامل، مشتری را می‌ترساند.
T.working_hook_en: A perfect five stars scares customers off.

key_sources.publisher: Medill Spiegel Research Center, Northwestern University
key_sources.claim: Purchase likelihood typically peaks at average ratings of 4.0-4.7 and declines as ratings approach 5.0 ('too good to be true'). A product with five reviews is 270% more likely to be bought than one with none. Sample size not stated on the page.

Dove 'r/eal Reviews': invited Redditors to try the Intensive Repair 10-in-1 Serum Hair Mask and published the first 50 reviews unedited, with permission, including negative ones (e.g. 'it kinda smells like expired hotel shampoo', which 'still made the campaign'), on NYC out-of-home, social and a Manhattan pop-up. Reported: over 1 billion impressions, hour-long pop-up queues, 150+ UGC pieces; mask sales up (no figure). Emily Barfoot: 'Transparency wasn't a risk. It was our strategy.'

48 male students heard a taped quiz candidate, high or average ability, with or without spilling coffee. The blunder raised liking for the highly capable candidate and lowered it for the average one; the blunder alone had no significant effect. A flaw only helps when competence is already clear.

H1 2026 best campaigns sold candour (Dove r/eal reviews won six Cannes Lions; Burger King retired its mascot; Aerie rejected AI content). Method1's Allison Arling-Giorgi: 'The pratfall effect basically allows you to admit a flaw.'

FTC complaints (allegations, not findings) in Oct 2026 include fabricated positive reviews and suppressing negative reviews (refunds conditioned on non-disparagement, fake BBB pages). Enforcement of the Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule is active.

T.framing_note: News is the spark (Oct 2026 FTC complaints over fabricated reviews and suppressed negative ones: allegations, caption-level only, do not name the alleged schemes on screen; Dove r/eal reviews won six Cannes Lions in June). The evergreen idea: a visible, small flaw makes the rest believable; a spotless record reads as edited. Be precise: Spiegel = purchase likelihood 'typically peaks' at 4.0-4.7, a 2017 analysis, sample not stated on the page: say 'research shows', never 'all customers'. Pratfall study 1966: 48 male students, taped quiz candidate; the flaw helped ONLY the highly capable candidate and hurt the average one: put this condition in the reel (scene ~5), it is the honest twist and the owner takeaway: be good first, then let the small flaw show. Dove results are Unilever self-reported (1bn+ impressions, queues, no sales figure); do not claim sales growth caused by it. Quote the review exactly: 'it kinda smells like expired hotel shampoo'. NEVER suggest inventing fake negative reviews or staged flaws (that is the same fakery the FTC is acting on). Practical close: don't delete the 3-star review; answer it; show what you changed. At most two numbers in the reel (4.7 / 5 as one comparison scene; optionally 50 reviews). Don't mock Dove or any brand. Never name the UAE, Dubai or any emirate.
